newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - FRENCH Q1 GDP UP 0.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - FRENCH Q1 GDP UP 0.2 PCT.

text.p: The following are financial analysts' comments after national statistics institute INSEE released data showing that French gross domestic product rose 0.2 percent from the previous quarter.
A Reuter poll of 11 economists had predicted a 0.4 percent rise.

I think the key thing here is stocks. A lot of people said dynamism at begining of year would lead to stock rebuilding. The point that I've been highlighting throughout is the effect of weak prices on stock building and it's one of the major risks to the growth outlook. Companies can't afford to build stocks if prices are edging down.

Obviously investment is the disappointment. It's difficult for an investment boom to take off before Q4 as capacity utilisation is so low, it needs a great leap of faith, they don't see that need to invest.

All of those (factors) suggest companies are very concerned about margins, about orders. I can't see a major...new dynamic force until the fourth quarter. I honestly don't see anything in the figures to think growth will exceed two percent this year.
We're off the bottom but people will be shocked at the slow speed were coming up given the length and depth of the downturn.

It's pretty much in line with our expectations. In our view it was the final quarter of a slow recovery trend which started in 1996. From here on we expect a strong acceleration in the second quarter and in the second half.
It's partly affected by the negative working days impact.
We've raised our forecast for the second quarter to five percent on an annualised basis, 1.2 percent quarter-on-quarter.
Our H2 (second half) forecast is unchanged at 2.5 percent (third quarter) and three percent (fourth quarter) on an annualised basis.

The figures are not as good as we expected. They confirm that the internal motor has not started. The weakest component was company investment, which is worrying as it is a factor blocking the recovery.
There has been a progression in household consumption and exports, which means there is a technical recovery but for it to be sustainable, there needs to be internal investment.
PHILIPPE BROSSARD, HEAD OF RESEARCH, ABN AMRO FINANCE.

The figures are disappointing. They are a reflection of the pessimism of industrialists with a drop in investment and a negative contribution from stocks, which INSEE explains by the (lower) number of working days.
